hypothesis: The training batch had only one wrong case (mqx-071), so this is a single example, not a measured pattern. The failure has a reasoning cause that will likely recur on other cases. The doctor got an abnormal objective finding (decreased hearing in both ears on exam) and dropped it because the patient said his hearing was fine. It submitted the close sibling diagnosis (vestibular neuritis) instead of labyrinthitis, which explains every finding. It also spent 3 of its 5 requests asking again for exam details it had already been told were 'not in the record', and never ordered audiometry, which would have settled it. In this setup, anything not in the case file comes back normal, so every abnormal result was put there on purpose and usually decides the answer. Fix: tell the doctor that abnormal findings are deliberate clues, and add a check it must do before submitting. The diagnosis must explain every abnormal finding. Objective findings beat the patient's own denials. Sibling diagnoses are decided by the feature that tells them apart. A 'not in the record' reply should not be re-requested; use the budget on a test that confirms the diagnosis instead.
changes: harness/system.md: added a 'How findings work' section. Abnormal findings are deliberate clues, and a 'not in the record' reply should not be re-requested in other words.

harness/system.md: added a mandatory pre-submit check. List all abnormal findings; the diagnosis must explain all of them; trust objective findings over the patient's own denials; pick the most specific diagnosis, using the feature that separates close siblings.

harness/lessons.md (was empty): three short general lessons. Build the diagnosis around a finding that conflicts with the patient's denial (neuritis vs labyrinthitis given as an example of the pattern). Before submitting, name the closest sibling diagnosis and check the finding that separates them. Spend leftover budget on tests that confirm the diagnosis rather than repeating requests for missing details.
expected_effect: I expect a small gain on held-out cases, though nothing has been run to confirm it. Where the answer depends on one abnormal finding separating two related diagnoses (neuritis vs labyrinthitis, and similar pairs elsewhere), the doctor should name the more specific entity the findings support. It should also order confirmatory tests instead of wasting requests. The cases that already pass should be unaffected: the instructions are short and only add a check before submitting. Combined system.md + lessons.md stays well under 16,000 characters, and config.json is unchanged.
